text:
maria: quick question — for the new internal inference fronting: do we want a thin REST->gRPC shim at the edge or invest in a gateway runtime that natively understands both?
jen: TL;DR: thin shim is faster to roll but more leaky for quotas/telemetry. gateway runtime buys us observability but is more ops-heavy.
mike: what are the hard constraints? latency SLOs for hosted API are 50ms p95 for short prompts. shim adds an extra hop; can we keep it <5ms?
sam: also think about quota propagation. With a shim we often lose caller identity unless we forward token headers and translate claims. That breaks per-route quota math in console.
maria: exactly — console needs token-level cost + route attribution for billing. If shim doesn't map attributes cleanly we end up with wrong cost buckets.
jen: one option: keep a tiny shim that preserves claims and injects an "x-rw-route" header. shim code: ```bash
# pseudo
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "x-rw-route: embeddings:v2" \
  http://internal-grpc-proxy/generate
```
mike: i like the header hack for quick rollout but it's brittle. What about telemetry? Datapoints we need: request.latency, model.token_count, cache.hit, routing.fallback. Gateway runtime can emit structured events so console can group by route/model/version.
sam: if we go gateway we can also implement smart routing (latency vs cost policies) without touching clients. That would let us do automated fallbacks to quantized variants under load.
maria: tradeoff is deploy complexity. Gateway requires schema for all routes (protobufs?) to validate and generate console UX. Do we standardize on proto definitions for public surfaces?
jen: yes, proto-first helps for typed payloads + smaller wire format for internal traffic. But browser clients still want JSON. So we'd need a transcoder in the gateway or a separate JSON facade.
mike: that brings us back to two-layer approach: gateway runtime inside data-plane (proto-native) + lightweight JSON facade at edge for browsers. Facade only handles translation and does no auth/quotas. Gateway enforces quotas.
sam: important: caching and batching semantics — gateway has access to KV cache and continuous batching. Facade shim would have to be cache-aware to avoid duplicate work. That's non-trivial.
maria: rollout plan idea: implement proto-first gateway on a single region for one non-critical endpoint (reranker) and run traffic via a shim to compare metrics. Canary signals: latency p95, cache hit ratio, quota mismatch rate, console attribution diffs.
jen: +1. Also add a regression test that checks attribute parity: for 100 sample requests assert route/model labels match between shim-path and gateway-path.
mike: ops note: gateway must expose a config endpoint for routing policies so SRE can tune cost vs latency. That needs RBAC and audit logs.
ops-bot: reminder: any gateway config changes will require a canary rollout and prometheus alerts: gateway.config.apply, gateway.errors.rate > 0.5% for 5m.
deploy-bot: canary job queued for realm-us-east-1, tag=proto-gateway-spike.
sam: last thought — documentation/console UX: if we move to proto-first we can auto-generate per-route dashboards (token-cost, latency, fallback-rate) from proto annotations. big win for product.
maria: ok next steps: jen + mike prototype a minimal proto schema + gateway prototype for reranker by EOD Friday. sam to draft canary metrics and parity tests. I'll sync with SRE on RBAC and rollout playbook.
jen: I'll push a tiny proto example to the repo and share link here so folks can eyeball shape.
mike: if anyone wants to play with the shim, see this toy snippet (node): ```js
// express shim
app.post('/v1/generate', async (req,res)=>{
  const headers = { 'x-rw-route': 'gen:v1', 'authorization': req.headers.authorization };
  const grpcResp = await grpcClient.generate({payload: req.body}, {metadata: headers});
  res.json(grpcResp);
});
```
maria: thanks — hoping we keep the shim as short-lived transitional piece and push to gateway runtime. will follow up in backlog ticket. :eyes:
